## TL;DR

Review round 1 found that the list-marker fix covered only the release notes, while Tailwind preflight strips markers from every rendered-markdown surface. I replaced the per-component rules with one shared rule in `style.css` that covers all six containers, and gave the playground the list indent it lacked. A table-driven test now guards each surface. The QA pass itself is unchanged: 135 headless WebKit checks against fixtures, with restart and dismiss verified only through faked endpoints.

## Work and rationale

The review was right that the defect class was wider than the one surface I fixed. Preflight resets every list to `list-style: none`, which removes markers while keeping `padding-left`. The first fix added markers only to `.release-update-markdown`. I could have added the same declaration to each of the five other surfaces, but that repeats the mistake the review named: the next markdown surface would regress again. So I put one selector list in `style.css`, next to the existing `.md-rendered` list rules, and added a comment pointing at the test that must stay in sync with it.

`.playground-markdown` had no list rule at all, so its lists had neither markers nor indent. I gave it the same 17 px indent as the pm and debugger surfaces, because restored markers would otherwise sit outside the bubble.

I moved the release-notes markers out of `ReleaseUpdateNotification.vue` and onto the shared rule, so there is one source of truth. The waiting line also moved from a selector that only matched the supervised layout to a `release-update-status` class, which the review had flagged as fragile. The class works in both the grid-based hand-run block and the supervised actions row.

## Approaches tried

I considered a stylelint-style check that scans every `.vue` file for `ul` rules. It would catch surfaces the table misses, but it is heavy and the repo has no CSS lint step. A static table of six surfaces, checked against the parsed CSS, is cheap and fails when someone drops a surface from the shared rule. The table comment says to add a new surface there, so the review's "next surface regresses" concern is handled by the rule's location and the test together.

Vitest returns an empty string for a CSS `?raw` import, so my first version of the test found no rules and failed six assertions. Reading `style.css` through `resolve(__dirname, ...)` matches the other UI tests and fixed it.

## Challenges and blockers

The QA harness reported one failed check on the first run after the shared rule. I did not capture which check it was. Three consecutive runs on the same final build passed 135 of 135 checks. I have recorded this as an unexplained flake in the QA doc rather than as resolved. A rerun would settle it, but the harness is headless and fixture-based, so the likeliest source is a timing check. I did not add a retry to hide it.

## Key learnings

- A fix for one markdown surface is a fix for the whole class. Review found five more surfaces with the same reset, so the durable form is one shared rule plus a surface table.
- Vitest does not return CSS content from `?raw`, so any test that greps `style.css` must read the file from disk.
- An unexplained single failure in a QA harness should be recorded as such, with the reruns, rather than dropped from the count.
